 The Honourable Sri Justice K.Surender
 Criminal Petition No.11247 Of 2023

entities.text: Vishwanathmaharshi ... vs The State Of Telangana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
This Criminal Petition is filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short 'Cr.P.C.') by the petitioner- Accused No.1 seeking to quash the proceedings against him in C.C.No.3039 of 2020 on the file of the III Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Nampally,
Hyderabad.

entities.text:
III Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Nampally,
Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The offences alleged against him are punishable under Sections 417, 420, 468 and 120-B of Indian Penal Code.
2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner - Accused No.1 and learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the respondent - State.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner confined his prayer to dispense with the personal appearance of petitioner - Accused No.1 before the trial Court.

4. Considering the submission of learned counsel for the petitioner, without going into the merits of the case, the attendance of the petitioner - Accused No.1 is dispensed with in C.C.No.3039 Crl.Petition No.11247 of 2023 of 2020 pending on the file of the III Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Nampally, Hyderabad, when represented by his counsel on record.

entities.text: III Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Nampally, Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The attendance of the petitioner - Accused No.1 is dispensed with subject to filing an affidavit by the petitioner stating that in his absence, the proceedings conducted by his counsel will not be disputed by him in any manner and shall not dispute his identity also.
However, the petitioner shall appear before the learned Magistrate as and when his presence is required.
In the event of failure of the petitioner to appear when the Court directs, this order dispensing his attendance shall stand cancelled.
5. Accordingly, the Criminal Petition is disposed of.

Needless to say, in the event of the petitioner filing an application seeking discharge, if charges are not framed, the concerned Court shall dispose of the same after hearing both sides, within a period of four (04) weeks.
Miscellaneous applications pending, if any, shall stand closed.

K.SURENDER, J Date: 16.11.2023 gvl Dr.Vishwanathmaharshi ... vs The State Of Telangana on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141857301/
